newsitem.title: USA: FINA to spend $6 million to restore marine habitat.
newsitem.headline: FINA to spend $6 million to restore marine habitat.

text.p: FINA Oil and Chemical Co and four of its contractors agreed to spend more than $6 million to settle allegations that they damaged about 40 acres of rare marine habitat near Corpus Christi, Texas, the Justice Department said Thursday.

The federal government sued the subsidiary of FINA Inc in 1992, saying it and the contractors destroyed 37 acres of seagrass and other habitat when they moved an oil rig in Laguna Madre, which is a bay separated from the Gulf of Mexico by Padre Island.

Under the agreement filed in U.S. District Court in Houston, the companies are to pay $2.28 million in civil fines, which the Justice Department said was the highest civil penalty ever imposed for unlawfully filling wetlands or other marine habitat.
The companies also are to restore the damaged seagrass beds and create another 37 acres of new seagrass habitat in the Laguna Madre at an estimated cost of $4 million.
If the agreement is approved by the court, it would settle the government's lawsuit, the department said.
